content: {"items":[{"passage_kind":"NARRATIVE_EVIDENCE","statement":"A series of coastal toponyms documented on maps or utilized in the modern vernacular of Phournoi are probably the living remnants of pirate activity in the past: Kourniachto (a place for hiding or lurking), Kleftolimano (harbor of thieves), Fygou (escape), Fylakio (guard-post), Vardia (shift or guard), Tourkolimnionas (harbor of the Turks), Pano and Kato Maneta (upper and lower Maneta).","evidence_id":"e-a651d645c92ef0849332","passage_ids":[9],"kind":"source_statement","source_type":"SECONDARY_SOURCE","actors":[],"places":["Phournoi","Kourniachto","Kleftolimano","Fygou","Fylakio","Vardia","Tourkolimnionas","Pano","Kato Maneta"],"dates":[],"usage_type":"RAID_LOCATION","uncertainty":["ORIGINAL_NOT_INSPECTED","SOURCE_GENEALOGY_PENDING","INDEPENDENCE_UNRESOLVED","TOPONYM_AND_USAGE_REQUIRE_SEMANTIC_EXTRACTION"]},{"passage_kind":"NARRATIVE_EVIDENCE","statement":"The two bays designated as Pano and Kato Maneta, situated roughly in the middle of the eastern coast of the main island of Phournoi, warrant further comment. It is highly probable that these two bays derived their names from the Zakynthian corsair Eustathios (Stathis) Romanos or Manetas, who, between 1678 and 1684, operated as a pirate in the Aegean Sea while based in Melos, commanding the only Greek privately owned corsair vessel at the time, most probably handed to him after the death of its former owner, the Maltese corsair Hugues Creviliers (Krantonelli 1994, 289–91).","evidence_id":"e-a651d645c92ef0849332","passage_ids":[11,12],"kind":"source_statement","source_type":"SECONDARY_SOURCE","actors":["Eustathios (Stathis) Romanos or Manetas","Hugues Creviliers"],"places":["Phournoi","Melos"],"dates":["1678","1684"],"usage_type":"BASE","uncertainty":["ORIGINAL_NOT_INSPECTED","SOURCE_GENEALOGY_PENDING","INDEPENDENCE_UNRESOLVED","TOPONYM_AND_USAGE_REQUIRE_SEMANTIC_EXTRACTION"]}]}
